_schema: Generated by scripts/gen_track_metrics_vectors.py from the Python track maths (src/models/track_edit.py, src/models/great_circle.py, _apportion_gain in src/project/repo_activities.py, the 'polyline' package). Do not edit by hand.
Each section is a list of {name, input, expected}; a case that must raise has expected_error (the Python exception name) instead of expected.
Compare floats within 1e-6; ints, strings, booleans and nulls exactly. Fields documented as int are written without a decimal point; all other numbers are doubles.

A point is [lat, lng, elev]; elev null = missing. A raw elevation outside [-20000, 20000] (or not finite) becomes null when the point is built, before any maths: the inputs use 65535 and -25000 for that.
haversine_km: input {lat1, lng1, lat2, lng2} degrees -> km, R = 6371.0.

polyline_encode: input {points: [[lat, lng], ...]} -> Google polyline, precision 5; null for no points (points_to_polyline). Each coordinate is scaled by 100000 and rounded HALF AWAY FROM ZERO (Dart's num.round), then delta-encoded.

align_points: input {summary_polyline: string|null, elevation_profile: {distances_km, elevations_m}|null} -> list of points. Elevation is interpolated by cumulative haversine distance along the decoded polyline, bisect_left over distances_km; before the first / past the last sample takes that sample. A missing, empty or length-mismatched profile gives every point elev null.
points_to_elevation_profile: input {points} -> {distances_km, elevations_m} or null when there are no points or no point has an elevation.

interpolate_elevation_gaps: input {distances_km, elevations (null = hole)} -> filled list. Leading/trailing holes take the nearest known value; interior holes are linear by distance, 0.0 fraction when the bracketing distances are equal.

run_stride: input {elevations} -> int. noise_estimate: input {elevations} -> {sigma: double, stride: int}. smooth_elevations: input {elevations, distances_km|null, sigma, stride: int} -> {smoothed, window}. noise_threshold: input {sigma, stride: int, window} -> double. These are elevation_gain's private helpers (_run_stride, _noise_estimate, _smooth_elevations, _noise_threshold).

elevation_gain: input {elevations, distances_km|null} -> expected double; 'diagnostics' {sigma, stride, window, threshold} are the helper values on the way (null for fewer than 2 elevations), for debugging a mismatch.

recompute_track_metrics: input {points, original_distance_m: double, original_moving_time: int, original_elapsed_time: int} (0.0/0/0 are the Python defaults, i.e. 'no originals') -> {distance (m), total_elevation_gain, elev_high, elev_low, start_latlng, end_latlng, average_speed, moving_time: int, elapsed_time: int}.
apportion_gain: input {stored: double|null, before, after} -> double.

sentinel_mask: input {elevations, distances_km} -> list of booleans, true where an exact 0.0 is the pre-#374 'no reading' sentinel (_sentinel_mask in alembic/versions/c4a9e1f70b38_repair_elevation_dropout_sentinel.py). Each maximal run of 0.0 is judged by its neighbour on each side that exists: step = |neighbour|, skipped when step < _SENTINEL_MIN_STEP_M; grade = step / (|distance between the neighbour and the run's nearest sample| * 1000), infinity when that distance is 0. The run is a dropout when the largest grade is strictly > _SENTINEL_MIN_GRADE; no grade (all-zero series, or steps too small) means real. Every sample false when the two lists differ in length. The repair then maps true samples to null and calls interpolate_elevation_gaps.

Python semantics to mirror: (1) recompute_track_metrics times are int(round(x)) with Python's round, i.e. HALF TO EVEN (2.5 -> 2, 3.5 -> 4), unlike Dart's round; the polyline encoder alone rounds half away from zero. (2) a median is the element at index len // 2 of the sorted list (the upper middle for an even length). (3) noise_estimate differences pair element i with i + stride; it stops as soon as an order has fewer than _NOISE_MIN_DIFFERENCES differences (even below order 3), samples every step-th difference with step = 1 + len // _NOISE_MEDIAN_SAMPLE_CAP, and keeps the smallest sigma over orders 3..5, 0.0 if none. (4) _NOISE_DIFFERENCE_SCALE[k] = 1.4826 / sqrt(C(2k, k)). (5) smoothing widens its window while d[i] - d[lo] > half_km and while d[hi+1] - d[i] <= half_km; it is skipped (window 1.0) for fewer than 3 samples or distances null / of another length. (6) gain books a rise when value - ref >= threshold and follows a fall when ref - value >= threshold. (7) recompute_track_metrics accumulates distance over every point but records elevation (with its cumulative distance) only for points that have one; elev_high/low are null when none has.
